newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares bounced back to close with slim gains as markets decided not to take the threat of a possible Japanese sale of U.S. Treasuries too seriously.
The AEX index of 25 blue chip shares closed 0.20 points higher at 861.06 after slumping more than 10 points at the opening after the Japanese prime minister had unsettled markets.
Many dealers said the rapid recovery in prices reflected the Dutch market's strength but some expressed worries about what they viewed as a persistent overbought condition.
"I was quite pleasantly surprised at how well the market held up," said one dealer.
"On the other hand the AEX and several individual stocks look heavily overbought and ripe for a correction," he added.
Most market participants said they did not expect the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee to raise interest rates when it meets next week on July 1 and 2.

Some said an unexpected rate hike could trigger a correction in share prices, but a minority said a small rise might help the market in the longer term by allaying fears about nascent inflationary pressures within the U.S. economy.
Among individual shares dealers noted that airline KLM had overcome resistance at 60.00, closing 0.70 firmer at 60.20.
Chemical group DSM posted a gain of 2.50 guilders at 193.50, helping to reverse a recent slide which saw the shares fall from over 200 guilders in May to below 190 last week.

Small-cap temporary employment firm Goudsmit closed 37.10 guilders or 13.8 percent higher at 306.00 after announcing plans to take over privately owned Unique in a move which would create a group with combined annual sales of some 600 million guilders.

Dealers said this would make Goudsmit the third biggest Dutch temp agency after Randstad and Vedior and that it might therefore command a higher price-earnings multiple, possibly lifting the shares as high as 400 guilders.
